title: A truth maintenance system
abstract: Introduces a truth-maintenance system that records justifications for beliefs and revises the active belief set when new discoveries contradict assumptions, while retaining dependency information useful for explanations and backtracking.

title: On the logic of theory change: Partial meet contraction and revision functions
abstract: Develops formal postulates and representation results for contraction and revision of belief theories, including partial-meet contraction, providing foundational machinery for distinguishing belief revision from simple addition or deletion.

title: An assumption-based TMS
abstract: Presents an assumption-based truth-maintenance system that represents alternative assumption sets, supports reasoning with inconsistent information and multiple contexts, and avoids destructive retraction of prior information.

title: Temporal Interpretation, Discourse Relations, and Commonsense Entailment
abstract: Provides a formal account of discourse relations and temporal relations between events using defeasible rules and commonsense knowledge, showing how similar surface forms can receive different temporal and discourse interpretations.

title: Discourse Obligations in Dialogue Processing
abstract: Models discourse obligations as dialogue attitudes that persist in conversational context, including obligations created by questions and other dialogue acts, providing a precursor to longitudinal commitment tracking.
venue: 32nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: A Consensus Glossary of Temporal Database Concepts
abstract: Defines and systematizes temporal-database concepts including distinctions needed to represent facts whose validity and database history vary over time, providing terminology relevant to valid-time versus observation or transaction-time reasoning.

title: Operational specification of a commitment-based agent communication language
abstract: Defines agent communication semantics through social commitments, including conditional commitments and precommitments, and specifies how communicative acts operate on commitment objects as interactions evolve.

title: Flexible protocol specification and execution: applying event calculus planning using commitments
abstract: Represents interaction protocols through commitments and uses event-calculus planning to reason about evolving social states, allowing agents more flexibility than protocols defined only as fixed action sequences.

title: TimeML: Robust Specification of Event and Temporal Expressions in Text
abstract: Defines TimeML for annotating events, temporal expressions, event-time anchoring, and temporal ordering across sentences and discourse, including underspecified temporal interpretations and modal contexts.
venue: AAAI Spring Symposium: New Directions in Question Answering

title: Classifying Temporal Relations Between Events
abstract: Studies automatic classification of temporal relations between textual events, combining event attributes with learned relation classifiers to support event ordering from natural language.

title: Jointly Combining Implicit Constraints Improves Temporal Ordering
abstract: Shows that temporal-relation predictions can be improved by joint inference that enforces implicit consistency constraints among relations instead of classifying each event pair independently.

title: Finding Contradictions in Text
abstract: Develops methods and a typology for recognizing textual contradictions, covering phenomena such as negation, antonymy, numeric differences, structural mismatches, and incompatible facts.

title: Provenance in Databases: Why, How, and Where
abstract: Surveys why-, how-, and where-provenance for database queries and their applications to confidence, updates, debugging, and annotation propagation, providing foundations for retaining derivational lineage rather than only current values.

title: Are You Sure That This Happened? Assessing the Factuality Degree of Events in Text
abstract: Models event factuality through polarity and degrees of certainty, addressing whether an event is presented as having happened, not happened, or remaining possible or uncertain.

title: Annotating Story Timelines as Temporal Dependency Structures
abstract: Represents story timelines as temporal dependency trees whose events are linked by relations such as BEFORE, AFTER, inclusion, identity, and overlap, with explicit treatment of modal, negated, and quoted contexts during event selection.

title: Extracting Narrative Timelines as Temporal Dependency Structures
abstract: Extracts narrative timelines by organizing events into temporal dependency structures rather than isolated pairwise relations, providing a structured representation of event ordering.

title: Joint Inference for Event Timeline Construction
abstract: Constructs event timelines with interval-based temporal representations and joint inference over local temporal classifiers, global constraints, and event-coreference information.

title: User Edits Classification Using Document Revision Histories
abstract: Uses document revision histories to distinguish factual edits from fluency edits, demonstrating that revision sequences can be classified according to the semantic significance of changes rather than only their lexical form.

title: Correction by adversative and additive markers
abstract: Analyzes linguistic correction expressed by adversative and additive markers and develops a semantic-pragmatic account of asymmetric and symmetric corrective constructions.

title: Corrective elaboration
abstract: Compares correction with elaboration and provides a unified pragmatic account in which discourse context and exhaustivity determine whether a subsequent utterance replaces an earlier alternative or elaborates it.

title: Automatically Classifying Edit Categories in Wikipedia Revisions
abstract: Develops automatic classification of Wikipedia revision edits into categories, providing empirical machinery for assigning semantic or functional meaning to changes across document versions.

title: FacTA: Evaluation of Event Factuality and Temporal Anchoring
abstract: Defines an evaluation task that explicitly connects event factuality profiling with temporal anchoring, bringing together whether an event is asserted as real and where it is situated temporally.

title: Knowledge-Based Trust: Estimating the Trustworthiness of Web Sources
abstract: Estimates source trustworthiness from the correctness of facts attributed to sources and uses joint inference to distinguish source factual errors from information-extraction errors.

title: Using Context to Predict the Purpose of Argumentative Writing Revisions
abstract: Predicts the purpose of revisions in argumentative writing using contextual information, contributing methods for classifying why a textual revision was made rather than merely detecting its surface change.

title: A Structured Learning Approach to Temporal Relation Extraction
abstract: Treats temporal-relation extraction as structured prediction so that dependencies and consistency among event-event relations are considered jointly, including the problem of missing temporal links.

title: Identifying Semantic Edit Intentions from Revisions in Wikipedia
abstract: Introduces a taxonomy of semantic intentions behind Wikipedia edits and trains a classifier to infer those intentions from revision data, moving beyond purely syntactic edit operations.

title: An Empirical Analysis of Edit Importance between Document Versions
abstract: Studies how important individual edits are when comparing successive document versions and models human judgments of whether changes are superficial or substantially alter document content or tone.

title: Tracking State Changes in Procedural Text: A Challenge Dataset and Models for Process Paragraph Comprehension
abstract: Introduces ProPara, a natural-language dataset in which entity existence and location must be tracked step by step through descriptions of changing processes, requiring inference of implicit state transitions.

title: Neural Ranking Models for Temporal Dependency Structure Parsing
abstract: Builds a neural temporal dependency parser that organizes textual events and time expressions into a temporal dependency tree and evaluates it on both news and narrative domains.

title: MultiFC: A Real-World Multi-Domain Dataset for Evidence-Based Fact Checking of Claims
abstract: Provides naturally occurring claims from multiple fact-checking domains together with textual evidence, metadata, and expert veracity labels, and jointly studies evidence ranking and claim-veracity prediction.

title: Do You Know That Florence Is Packed with Visitors? Evaluating State-of-the-art Models of Speaker Commitment
abstract: Evaluates speaker-commitment and event-factuality models on naturally occurring discourse, showing that commitment depends on linguistic context such as negation, modality, questions, and conditionals.

title: Inherent Disagreements in Human Textual Inferences
abstract: Shows that disagreement about natural-language inference often persists rather than disappearing as annotation noise and argues that models should preserve distributions of plausible judgments rather than force a single interpretation.
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Tracking Discrete and Continuous Entity State for Process Understanding
abstract: Tracks evolving entity states through procedural text with a model combining recurrent continuous representations and globally constrained discrete states, enforcing consistency across process steps.
venue: Third Workshop on Structured Prediction for NLP

title: Fact or Fiction: Verifying Scientific Claims
abstract: Introduces scientific claim verification in which systems retrieve evidence-containing abstracts, decide whether evidence supports or refutes a claim, and identify the rationale for that decision.

title: Exploring Contextualized Neural Language Models for Temporal Dependency Parsing
abstract: Evaluates contextualized neural language models for temporal dependency parsing, which links events and time expressions into document-level temporal structures rather than treating temporal relations independently.

title: A Dataset for Tracking Entities in Open Domain Procedural Text
abstract: Introduces OPENPI, where systems generate open-vocabulary tuples describing an entity, changed attribute, before-state, and after-state at each step of natural procedural text.

title: HoVer: A Dataset for Many-Hop Fact Extraction And Claim Verification
abstract: Requires systems to gather evidence distributed across multiple documents and determine whether a claim is supported, providing a testbed for corroborative reasoning over several evidence sources.

title: Get Your Vitamin C! Robust Fact Verification with Contrastive Evidence
abstract: Builds a fact-verification benchmark from Wikipedia revisions that change underlying facts, pairing near-identical but factually contrasting evidence and explicitly testing sensitivity to evidence that changes over time.

title: Factuality Assessment as Modal Dependency Parsing
abstract: Frames event factuality as modal dependency parsing that jointly identifies events, their source or conceiver, and the certainty with which each source commits to those events.

title: Identifying inherent disagreement in natural language inference
abstract: Distinguishes NLI cases with systematic agreement from cases with genuine annotation disagreement and models multiple plausible interpretations instead of collapsing all examples to a single certain label.

title: One Document, Many Revisions: A Dataset for Classification and Description of Edit Intents
abstract: Provides full Wikipedia revision histories annotated for edit intent and studies both classification of revision purposes and generation of free-form descriptions of changes across document versions.

title: Investigating Reasons for Disagreement in Natural Language Inference
abstract: Develops a taxonomy of sources of disagreement in natural-language inference and evaluates modeling approaches that retain multiple possible labels when evidence or interpretation does not warrant a single resolved judgment.
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Event Semantic Knowledge in Procedural Text Understanding
abstract: Studies entity-state tracking in procedural text and injects event-semantic knowledge to infer changes that are often implicit in verbs and commonsense process descriptions.

title: Discourse Information for Document-Level Temporal Dependency Parsing
abstract: Examines document-level temporal dependency parsing with discourse and sentence-position information, constructing temporal dependency graphs across a document rather than isolated event pairs.

title: Re3: A Holistic Framework and Dataset for Modeling Collaborative Document Revision
abstract: Introduces a framework linking document revisions, reviews, and author responses, with aligned scientific-paper revisions labeled by revision action and intent and accompanied by reviews and edit summaries.

title: ECON: On the Detection and Resolution of Evidence Conflicts
abstract: Studies detection and resolution of conflicts between pieces of evidence, evaluating NLI, factual-consistency models, and LLMs and showing that conflict resolution can select one source without an adequate evidential justification.

title: What Evidence Do Language Models Find Convincing?
abstract: Introduces ConflictingQA, pairing contentious queries with real-world evidence documents that disagree in facts and answers, and examines which evidence characteristics influence model arbitration under conflict.

title: ProPara-CRTS: Canonical Referent Tracking for Reliable Evaluation of Entity State Tracking in Process Narratives
abstract: Introduces a canonical referent tracking schema in which surface mentions map to immutable discourse referents whose existence and location are recorded at each process step, supporting more reliable longitudinal state histories.

title: When Text and Numbers Disagree: Evidence Arbitration in Large Language Models
abstract: Uses a controlled synthetic benchmark with conflicting textual and numerical evidence to test arbitration while independently varying temporal recency, source reliability, modality, and provenance; the study finds systematic evidence-selection heuristics rather than reliable provenance-sensitive resolution.
